newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina, Haiti to boost political, economic ties.
newsitem.headline: Argentina, Haiti to boost political, economic ties.

text.p: Argentina's President Carlos Menem and President Rene Preval of Haiti on Tuesday agreed to promote bilateral political and economic ties.

Preval, on a two-day visit, was the first Haitian president to visit Argentina. At a joint news conference Menem praised him "for the efforts made by the government and people of Haiti to consolidate democracy and to rebuild the economy."
Menem said his government would continue supporting the Haitian government in its efforts.
In 1994 a U.S.-led invasion ousted a military dictatorship and restored Jean-Bertrand Aristide as president. Preval is Aristide's successor.

Preval thanked Argentina for its recent decision to annul 85 percent of Haiti's debt with Argentina. This showed "more than Argentina's willingness to contribute to the development of Haiti." Haiti is the poorest country in the Americas.

The presidents promised to "strengthen still further the politicial dialogue, cooperation and the bonds of friendship." They also underscored the need to fight drug trafficking and condemned "international terrorism in all its forms."
